C0.quote: a voting rule is guaranteed to output a valid ranking
C0.note: Borderline: this is truth discovery for crowdsourcing, close to the codebook's 'ML rank aggregation' exclusion. It is coded ELIG because workers' rankings are aggregated by (weighted) voting rules and Theorem 7 concerns weighted Kemeny; ELIG is the first-listed code under doubt.

C1.quote: Our main conceptual result is an approximately linear connection
C1.note: Main results are statistical estimation results (Anna Karenina principle, MLE optimality of weighted Kemeny under Condorcet noise), plus synthetic and real-data evaluation.

C2.2.note: General framework also covers binary vectors, real-valued and arbitrary labels (OTH).

C2.3.quote: The type ti of a worker determines her distribution of answers.
C2.3.note: The held attitude is a type (competence), not a preference.

C2.4.quote: the report of worker i is a random variable si sampled
C2.4.note: The type ti and the report si are separate objects, with the report drawn as noise from the type.

C3.1.note: Strategic behaviour is mentioned only as a shortcoming and future work.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used for voters; only fault and competence.

C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by accuracy against the ground truth, not by welfare.
